messages:
Elaine: Heads-up — customer X sent a 60-question security questionnaire and flagged three must-haves: strict RBAC change approvals, 1yr audit log retention with tamper-proof export, and a runbook for vuln->incident escalation. Can we confirm current gaps?
Mike: Thanks, sharing the doc now. Quick answers: RBAC approvals are manual today (ok for small teams), we do immutable audit logs in the DB but no signed export flow to S3. Retention is configurable per-tenant but defaults to 90d.
Sara: @Mike @Elaine this feels like two tracks: (1) short-term answers for the questionnaire, (2) product work (RBAC approval workflow + signed export + retention policy defaults). I can own the Q responses. Need precise wording for 'tamper-proof export' — customer expects evidence of chain-of-custody.
Jules: For chain-of-custody we can provide signed manifests + S3 object-lock + KMS envelope proof. We have HSM-backed KMS in Private but hosted uses cloud KMS — both can sign export manifests.
Elaine: Can you sketch the minimal export command and manifest format we can ship this week? Customer wants examples.
Jules: Minimal shim: create an export job -> write logs to s3://redwood-custX-exports/YYYYMMDD/ -> generate manifest.json with SHA256 list -> sign manifest with KMS (Sign API) -> put manifest.sig alongside. Example:```bash
# run on export host
aws s3 cp /tmp/audit-20250301.json s3://redwood-custX-exports/20250301/audit.json
sha256sum audit.json > audit.json.sha256
aws kms sign --key-id alias/exports-key --message fileb://audit.json.sha256 --output text --query Signature | base64 -d > manifest.sig
aws s3 cp manifest.sig s3://redwood-custX-exports/20250301/
```
Mike: That looks good. For hosted customers we may need to rotate the export key per-export and record key-id in the manifest for verification. Also add S3 Object Lock "GOVERNANCE" + bucket versioning.
Sara: For the questionnaire wording: we can say "signed export manifests produced using KMS Sign; exports stored in S3 with versioning and Object Lock; verification steps provided." Keep it non-prescriptive re: kms provider.
Elaine: On RBAC approvals: customer asks for approval chain + attestation on privileged role changes. We have audit trails but no approval workflow. Options?
Jules: Short-term: require PR + 2 approvers on infra repo (enforced by branch protection) and attach PR link to role change tickets in Jira. Medium-term: add built-in "role-change request" API with approver list + signed approval event in audit log.
Mike: Also add drift detection to catch out-of-band changes — a nightly job that diff current IAM bindings vs expected. If drift found, create an alert to sec-oncall and open a ticket.
Elaine: Can we show a sample drift alert payload? Customer wants an example of evidence.
Mike: Example payload (short):```json
{ "tenant": "custX", "when": "2025-03-01T03:00:00Z", "diffs": [ {"path":"/roles/admin","change":"added","principal":"svc-legacy"} ], "snapshot_s3":"s3://redwood-custX-exports/20250301/iam-snapshot.json" }
```
Sara: Good. We'll include that as an appendix. Also need to document oncall responsibilities: who acknowledges, who remediates, SLA targets. Proposed flow: ack within 1h, initial triage 4h, mitigation or rollback 24h (or as per customer risk matrix).
Elaine: Customer also asked about vuln triage -> incident escalation. We should tie Severity scoring to action and evidence retention. Any existing playbook we can link?
Jules: We have a draft playbook in Confluence: /sec/playbooks/vuln-to-incident. It has triage steps + PoC handling + disclosure timeline. I'll link it in the response.
DevOps Bot: Reminder: export jobs will be queued on the analytics cluster; expected completion ~10-30m depending on log size.
Mike: One more ask: customer wants proof of periodic key rotation policy and logs of KMS access. We log every Sign/Decrypt request to our audit stream; retention currently 90d unless exported. For the questionnaire we'll provide sample log lines (timestamp, key-id, caller, action, request-id).
Elaine: Perfect. Sara, can you draft the questionnaire answers and attach the examples: (1) export command + manifest example, (2) drift alert JSON, (3) sample KMS access lines, (4) proposed RBAC approval short-term and roadmap? Aim to send by EOD PST.
Sara: On it. I'll ping @Jules for the manifest signing snippet and @Mike for the drift snapshot S3 link.
Jules: Sending snippets now in thread, will also include verification steps (how customer can validate manifest.sig with public key).
Mike: I'll trigger a prototype nightly drift run for custX and post the first snapshot link here. :thumbsup:
Elaine: Thanks team — this should close most of their asks. We'll follow up with a call if they want to walk the proofs.
